svg.aria-label: WHAT: the transform never sees the window rule
svg.text: What and Where as two arguments — one function, nine pipelines
2 // Two of an event's five fields are CLOCKS, which ch01 established:
3 // et = event time, when it happened · pt = processing time, when we saw it
4 // v = the value being summed · key = which stream it belongs to
5 type Event { id, key, et, pt, v }
6 // primitive: EVENTS — the book's 9 events, in PROCESSING order (tools/stream_seed.js).
7 // EVENTS[7] = (id 7, key "b", et 50, pt 280, v 4) <- the late one
8 // primitive: NONE — no value. Distinct from a value of 0.
9 // primitive: WIN — the fixed window width, in seconds of event time. WIN = 120
10 // primitive: LAG — the watermark's assumed worst-case skew. LAG = 60
11 // primitive: W0 — the window this chapter specifies. W0 = 0 ([12:00, 12:02))
12 // primitive: winOf(et) — the START of the WIN-second event-time window holding et.
14 // primitive: sum(ids) — total v over those event ids.
16 // primitive: append(xs, x) — xs with x added at the end. append([1], 2) = [1,2]
20 // primitive: PERIOD — how often a sliding window starts. PERIOD = 60
21 // primitive: windowsOf(et, where) — EVERY window an event belongs to. Note the
22 // return is a LIST: overlapping windowings put one event in more than one.
26 // primitive: apply(what, ids) — run the transform over those event ids.
31 // function: assign(events, where) — group every event under its window(s).
32 // This answers WHERE and nothing else: no transform is named anywhere in it.
45 // function: compute(grouped, what) — run ONE transform over every group.
46 // This answers WHAT and nothing else: no window rule appears in it.
56 // function: totalOf(r) — add up every window's result.
60 for (w in r.byWindow) { t = t + r.byWindow[w] }
64 // function: main() — THE CALLER: two axes, chosen separately.
Step 2/0 — WHAT: the transform never sees the window rule
`compute` receives an already-grouped Result and a transform name. It has no idea whether those groups came from fixed, sliding or session windows —
`apply("count", [0, 1, 2, 7])` = 4 would be identical either way. That is what "independent axes" means mechanically.
